report:
Urinary bladder, prostate and seminal vesicles, radical cystoprostatectomy

Received in formalin is a radical cystoprostatectomy specimen measuring 12.5 x 9.5 x 7.0 cm. Opening the bladder shows a mucosal scar / ulcerated area without a definite residual gross mass. Attached organs: prostate and seminal vesicles grossly unremarkable. Sections are submitted in 18 blocks.

(A1-A2) right and left ureteral margins.
(A3) urethral margin.
(A4-A11) bladder tumour full thickness with perivesical fat.
(A12-A14) representative bladder mucosa.
(A15-A16) prostate and seminal vesicles.
(A17-A18) bilateral pelvic lymph nodes.

Specimen and tumour
- Procedure: Radical cystoprostatectomy
- Tumour site: Right lateral wall and posterior wall
- Tumour configuration: Ulcerated

Microscopic findings
- Histologic type: No residual carcinoma identified (pT0)
- Associated urothelial carcinoma in situ (UCIS): Not identified
- Tumour extension (depth of invasion): No residual primary tumour (pT0)
- Prostatic involvement (if cystoprostatectomy): Not identified
- Lymphovascular invasion: Not identified
- Tumour histology:
  Extensive sampling of the tumour bed shows fibrosis, chronic inflammation and therapy-related changes with no residual carcinoma identified.

Margins
- Surgical margins: All margins uninvolved by invasive carcinoma and CIS
  - Right ureteral margin: Uninvolved by invasive carcinoma and CIS
  - Left ureteral margin: Uninvolved by invasive carcinoma and CIS
  - Urethral margin: Uninvolved by invasive carcinoma and CIS
  - Perivesical soft tissue margin: Uninvolved by invasive carcinoma
- Distance to closest margin: 8 mm (right posterolateral perivesical soft
  tissue)

Lymph nodes
- Regional lymph nodes: 0 of 18 involved (bilateral pelvic (obturator and
  external iliac))

Pathological stage (AJCC 8th edition)
- pTNM: ypT0 ypN0

Additional findings
- Additional pathologic findings: Therapy-related changes (fibrosis / giant cell
  reaction)
